subject: HealthGrid DPA: derivative rights exclusion + cross-border evidence request
messages:
From: Matt O'Neil <matt.oneil@healthgrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on derivative/learning exclusion + next steps

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and control features look promising. Before Legal proceeds we have a couple of follow-ups on the DPA draft:

1) We asked for a clear "no-derivatives / no-learning" commitment for prompt + response pairs. Can you confirm how that maps to your internal subsystems (caching, telemetry, feature flags) and whether that can be scoped to this account only?

2) We also need an evidence pack showing where (which subprocessors, regions) any transient prompt/response content is stored, and the plan for cross-border transfers. A CSV manifest with subprocessors, purpose, and residency would be ideal.

If you can point me to an existing template or example evidence pack, that will speed things up. Can we get an initial reply by Friday (7/31)?

Best,
Matt
Product Ops | HealthGrid

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Matt O'Neil <matt.oneil@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on derivative/learning exclusion + next steps

Matt — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, and then next steps: 

- No-learning commitment: yes — we can commit that prompt/response pairs submitted to your tenant will not be used to update or fine-tune any models or shared datasets. That applies to the hosted tenant used by HealthGrid and can be enforced via tenant-level configuration (we will add the "no_model_improvement" flag to your account).

- Subprocessors / residency: we keep short-lived telemetry and traces for operational debugging (TTL 72 hours by default) unless longer retention is requested and agreed. Persistent storage for customer content is optional and only used for features you opt into (e.g., audit export). We can provide a CSV manifest listing the processors involved (cloud provider storage, logging/observability vendors, S3 buckets used for export).

Next steps I'd propose:
- Marissa to share the minimal evidence pack template we use for SOC2 / DPA reviews (subprocessor manifest + retention table).
- Dev to confirm exactly which tables/streams the no_training flag gates, and draft a brief ops runbook we can include in the evidence pack.
- We'll send a redline-friendly DPA excerpt with the explicit no-derivatives clause for your legal review.

Target: send the evidence pack + DPA excerpt by EOD Friday (7/31). If that's tight for you, tell us and we'll move to Monday.

Hannah
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@healthgrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on derivative/learning exclusion + next steps

Hannah — thanks, that helps. Attached are a few DPA redlines (see redlines_20260730.pdf) we expect to land on, plus a short list of clarifying questions from our side:

- Can you define "prompt/response pairs" precisely for contract language? Does it include system messages, tool outputs, and metadata?
- We want to ensure the no-learning commitment covers any downstream feature experiments (e.g., embeddings recalculation, search ranking models) that HealthGrid might rely on.
- For the evidence pack, we need per-subprocessor country of processing and whether data crosses regions during transient processing.

We prefer the evidence manifest as CSV and a short summary page (one pager) that calls out any exceptions. Also happy to hop on a quick 30-minute call if useful.

—Lena
Senior Counsel, Privacy | HealthGrid

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Matt O'Neil <matt.oneil@healthgrid.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on derivative/learning exclusion + next steps

Hi Matt / Lena — attaching the evidence pack stub as discussed and a short ops runbook excerpt. See attachments: evidence_pack_minimal_manifest.csv (contains subprocessors, purpose, country, residency notes) and runbook_no_training.md (excerpt describing gated subsystems). Highlights: 

- The no_model_improvement flag prevents data from entering model-training pipelines and from being used to update embedding indexes or search rerankers by default.
- Telemetry/trace retention: default 72 hours; optional 90-day retention only by signed request and we document that in the DPA addendum.
- Cross-border: primary processing for HealthGrid is in us-west-2; observability vendor processes in EU for infra metrics only (no customer content). The CSV marks these rows and includes a boolean column "cross_border_possible".

Attachments referenced in-line: 1) evidence_pack_minimal_manifest.csv 2) runbook_no_training.md 3) proposed_dpa_excerpt.txt

If you'd like, we can do a 30-minute call on Tuesday to walk through the manifest and the exact phrasing of the proposed DPA clause. Would 10:00 AM PT work?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
